notes: §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR2: 'Its PICTURE character-string can contain only the symbol 'A'' and 'Its content, when represented in standard data format, must be one or more alphabetic characters.' AnalyzeCharacterString's A/X arm sets IsAlphabetic exactly when every expanded symbol is 'A' (no edition arm: the picture rule is the same in every edition), so PIC A9A or PIC AB is alphanumeric or alphanumeric edited, never alphabetic; TryExpandRepeats refuses A(0) (COBOL2147), so the item holds one or more positions. Sentence b binds the content the program stores, and the compiler serves it through the category: Table16Operand reads IsAlphabetic, so a numeric literal, a numeric item or a numeric edited item moved to PIC AAA, and PIC AAA moved to a numeric item, are refused (COBOL0819, probed at --std 85). The 1985 bar on the NUMERIC class test of an alphabetic item is another rule's and is open as kb/Work PB5122. The witness stores and displays two alphabetic values in PIC AAAAA.

next.reason: 1985: an alphabetic PICTURE 'can contain only the symbol A' and its content 'must be one or more alphabetic characters' (GR8: 'A' 'can contain only an alphabetic character'). §2023:13.18.40.4 GR5 keeps the picture rule ('shall contain only one or more occurrences of the symbol A'), but §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14 makes each 'A' 'a character position that shall contain any character from the computer's alphanumeric character set' ('equivalent to the symbol X except within the execution of a VALIDATE statement'). Content requirement loosened; only VALIDATE checks it as alphabetic.
